thread:
anna: customer reported 504s and long timeouts during a sudden tenant spike (~11:23 UTC). They saw gateway timeouts while requests were waiting in the inference queue. Sample request_id: req_0a1b2c. Raising for triage /cc @maya @samir :warning:

maya: checking telemetry now. I see a big enqueue backlog on request-scheduler and only 2 model pods serving; HPA desiredReplicas stayed at 2. KEDA scaledobject events show multiple cooldowns and a couple readiness failures.

samir: digging into k8s:
```
kubectl get hpa -n inference model-worker-hpa
NAME                 REFERENCE                 TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
model-worker-hpa     Deployment/model-worker   cpu 50%    2         20        2
```
events for ScaledObject: `Scale event ignored: cooldown active` then `Scale failed: readiness probe failed for pod model-worker-abc`

jonah: looked at pod init logs for model-worker-abc: model fetch + quantize step took ~32s and readiness probe threshold is 30s, so pod never marked ready and KEDA aborts scale. excerpt: `INFO model_loader: fetching weights (size=4.8GB)`, `INFO model_loader: quantize step completed in 28s`, `WARN readiness_probe: startup exceeded 30s`

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1247, priority P2, assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

anna: customer describes repeated 504s and manual retries helped. They want root cause and quick mitigation.

maya: probable chain: tenant spike -> request-scheduler backlog -> KEDA tries to scale -> new pods hit cold-init > readiness timeout -> KEDA cooldown prevents immediate retry -> observed 504s at gateway. Two levers: reduce cold-init time or make autoscaler tolerate longer startup.

samir: quick mitigation options I can apply now: 1) bump HPA minReplicas from 2->4 to absorb burst, 2) extend readinessProbe startupSeconds to 120, 3) temporarily route this tenant to dedicated capacity (if available). Which do we want?

jonah: prefer low-risk first: increase minReplicas to 4 for model-worker and increase KEDA cooldown to 15s -> but cooldown likely already blocking, better to increase minReplicas + add `redwood.dev/prewarm: "true"` annotation on deployment to enable prefix cache preload. I'll prepare quick patch.

anna: customer prefers minimal change that fixes SLA. They asked about costs — we told them brief increase in capacity. Go ahead with minReplicas bump and prewarm.

maya: applied helm patch -> set replicaCount min to 4 and annotated deployment. Also raised readinessProbe.timeoutSeconds from 30->120. Commands run:
```
helm upgrade inference -f overrides.yaml charts/inference \ 
  --set modelWorker.minReplicas=4 \ 
  --set modelWorker.annotations.redwood.dev/prewarm="true"
kubectl patch deployment model-worker -n inference -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","readinessProbe":{"timeoutSeconds":120}}]}}}}'
```

samir: monitoring: queue drained within ~45s after change, 504s dropped to near-zero for that tenant. We should still root cause why model-init is long: large model file fetch from remote blobstore, and quantize path takes long on cold start.

jonah: action items: 1) eng-runtime: investigate cold-start optimizations (streaming load, smaller quantized variants) — owner: jonah. 2) infra: evaluate using prewarmed pool or model cache on nodes — owner: maya. 3) support: follow up with customer about temporary capacity bump and cost impact — owner: anna.

anna: noted, I'll update the customer and close once follow-up confirmed. Thanks team :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: update: incident INC-2026-1247 status -> mitigated (P2)
